changes.summary: Throwback Week wasn't throwing all the way back on the Set Lineup screen. Week 4 correctly gave both teams their old names and their old colors, then painted the modern logo behind the players anyway — so the Pigskins, whose throwback name is just 'Pacific Pigskins' again, showed no sign of throwing back at all. The crest was the one piece of the old identity nobody had wired up: the overlay swapped the team's icon, but that banner reads a different field, and that field kept pointing at today's mark. It now wears the era's own logo, and each team's 2013-or-whenever crest sits behind its player like it was supposed to.

The matchup banner on Set Lineup was showing you the same two faces every week, and both of them were quarterbacks. It picked whoever projected highest, and since a starting QB projects ten points clear of anyone else on a roster, the tight end who is the best tight end in football never once got the panel. It now casts by rank within position, weighed against how many the league actually has to start — we start one quarterback and four backs and receivers, so QB12 is a guy you'd bench where WR12 is a stud, and the panel finally knows the difference. The line under the name says which — WR1 · CIN · 18.0 PROJ — so you can see why that face is up there. Thirteen of sixteen teams get a new headliner out of it, and a genuinely elite quarterback still gets his panel. The two headshots also moved out to the far edges of the banner instead of standing in the middle of it, which finally lets your franchise crest read behind them instead of being a rumor.

Schefter dropped a Pecking Order on the AFL in the middle of August, ranking a season that ended in December. The column runs every Tuesday year-round and it knew to sit out the offseason — it just had no idea it was the offseason. Its season clock rolls at Labor Day, so from February until then it still answers '2025', and the last completed week of 2025 is, unhelpfully, always available. The only thing that had kept it quiet all summer was that every past week already had a column on file; the first gap in the archive is what let it write one and buzz everybody's phone. It now checks that the season it's about to rank is actually being played, so the earliest column of any year is the Tuesday after Week 1, and the stray August issue has been pulled.

Set Lineup had two ways of losing your lineup on a future week, and an owner caught both in the same sitting: week 12 came up with nine empty slots and week 14 came up with nine players named 'Player 13592'. The names were the easy half — every page view re-asked MFL for the whole player file, and when that call got throttled the page had nothing left to print but the ID, even though the same names are sitting in a feed on our own disk. The empty week was the same throttling hitting the roster call instead. But the real find was underneath: the page asked MFL for your saved lineup with a request MFL has never accepted — myStarters is an import, not an export — and the error was swallowed, so it silently fell back to filling the slots with whoever projects best. That means it has never once shown you a lineup you submitted. It does now, for any week, and when there's genuinely nothing on file for that week it says so instead of dressing up a projection as your lineup.
